newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico refining project to cut gasoline imports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico refining project to cut gasoline imports.

text.p: State owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) announced on Tuesday projects at its Cadereyta refinery aimed at making better use of a glut of heavy crude and at reducing gasoline imports.
With a total investment of almost $1.2 billion in the northern refinery, Pemex said it will build ten new plants, expand six plants and modernize another six plants.

The project "will allow increased production of gasoline, diesel and keroseines, reduce the production of fuel oil and satisfy the established specifications in environmental norms," Pemex said in a statement.
Mexico imported 69,000 barrels per day (bpd) of gasoline in 1996, mostly from the United States, while exporting just 23,000 bpd of gasoline.
The project will aim to shrink high sulfur fuel oil output to encourage the use of natural gas as a substitute, the statement said.

Expansion at the Cadereyta complex, which alternates between the nation's second and third largest refinery, also is expected to boost refining of heavy Maya crude to 270,000 bpd from 235,000 bpd, Pemex said.
Greater heavy crude output and a slide in demand has produced an international glut.

One of the new plants that has already begun operation will eventually produce 6,000 bpd of alkalines in a move to reduce the import of high octane gas for an estimated savings of $3.6 million per month.
